Soraya: ...How many secrets does Liyue truly hold?

column1: Traveler: Do you mean buried treasure?

column1: Soraya: This place we are in is called the Guili Assembly. According to Liyue folklore
column2: it was once inhabited by people — in fact
column3: it was rather prosperous.

column1: Soraya: But for various reasons
column2: the whole place was wiped out. All that remains now is the countless ruins scattered across the landscape.

column1: Soraya: Some stories put it down to conflict between the gods

column3: catastrophic natural disaster...

column3: the Treasure Hoarders...

column1: Soraya: ...And masochistic scholars
column2: like me
column3: who in spite of all the risks just can't resist the idea of how much research value these ruins have to offer.

column1: Soraya: In practice though

column3: and I already need a rest...

column1: Traveler: Sure.

column2: but I should give you an idea of what to look for... Yes
column3: keep your eyes peeled for stone pillars and stone tablets.

column1: Soraya: Given how ancient these ruins are
column2: any text we can hope to find will be written on stone
column3: not paper.

column1: Soraya: After all
column2: stone is the oldest and most durable medium for written communication.

column1: Traveler: What am I looking for?

column2: that means looking for stone pillars and stone tablets.

column1: Soraya: Stone is the oldest
